source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Social/Political Life Ch. 2 (Grassroots Democracy – Part 1).

sections.heading: 1. What is Governance
points: **Governance** = the way a society is **run** — making rules and decisions, and putting them into practice for the common good.
A **government** is the group of people and institutions given the authority to govern.
Governance provides **order, services and justice**, and settles disputes fairly.

sections.heading: 2. Why We Need Government
points: To make and enforce **rules/laws** so people live together peacefully.
To provide **public services** — roads, water, electricity, schools, hospitals, sanitation.
To ensure **safety and security** and to **resolve conflicts** justly.
To take decisions for the **whole community**, which individuals cannot do alone.

sections.heading: 3. Democracy
points: **Democracy** = government **by the people** — often described as "of the people, by the people, for the people."
People **elect** their representatives through **voting (elections)**.
Decisions are taken by **discussion, participation and majority**, while respecting **everyone's rights**.
Key values: **equality, participation, accountability** and respect for all.

sections.heading: 4. Levels of Government in India

sub: **Local government** — panchayats (villages) and municipalities (towns/cities); closest to people.

points: Each level has its own responsibilities and works within the **Constitution**.

sections.heading: 5. Grassroots Democracy
points: **"Grassroots"** = the **local level**, where democracy is closest to ordinary people.
At this level people can directly take part in decisions about their village or town.
The **Panchayati Raj** system (villages) and urban local bodies make democracy work at the grassroots (detailed in Parts 2 and 3).

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Governance = running society (making + enforcing decisions); government = who does it.
Democracy = government by the people; "of the people, by the people, for the people."
People choose representatives through elections (voting).
Three levels of government: Local → State → Union (Central).
Grassroots = local level; Panchayati Raj = rural local government.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: India has **three** levels of government — local, state and union.
**Grassroots democracy = local level**, not the central government.
In a democracy, majority rule must still **respect everyone's rights** — it is not simply 'the majority does anything'.
